title: Running apps to log your activities
description: Compare ways to record runs, review routes and follow audio-guided sessions.
intro: These apps offer different approaches to recording or reviewing a run. The descriptions below are based on the providers’ own documentation, not hands-on testing or a ranking. Check device compatibility, permissions, privacy settings and current subscription terms before choosing one.

entries.name: adidas Running
entries.description: The provider lists GPS tracking, run statistics and a voice coach among its features. It also describes challenges and training plans; verify which features are currently available in your region and plan.

entries.name: ASICS Runkeeper
entries.description: Runkeeper says its phone app uses GPS to record distance, duration, pace and a map of the route. Its getting-started guide explains that a OneASICS account is needed to sign in.

entries.name: Garmin Connect
entries.description: Garmin describes Connect as a place to review activity information recorded on a Garmin device and compare past runs. Unlike a phone-only recording app, this option is oriented around a compatible Garmin device.

entries.name: Nike Run Club
entries.description: Nike’s getting-started guide describes tracking runs and using audio-guided runs. Review the app’s location and fitness-tracking permissions if you want to use its tracking features.

entries.name: Strava
entries.description: Strava’s mobile recording guide describes GPS-based activities with map and statistics views, including pace information during a run. Review audience and location privacy settings before sharing an activity.
